html: In this stunning portrait, the Montreal-based filmmaker and photographer Sarah Seené captures the world of her friend Marie-Christine Ricignuolo, who lost most of her sight to congenital glaucoma several years ago at the age of 30. A comedian and actress who also tours as a public speaker, Ricignuolo reflects thoughtfully on her relationships with her partner, her son and the world she now interacts with quite differently – through memories, her limited sight and, above all, touch. Seené translates that sensory experience through analogue film, which she reworks with experimental processes to produce footage that is textured and ethereal, where even mundane events like a visit to the optician take on a strange beauty. The result is at once moving and inspiring, showing how, with the loss of even one of our most important senses, our capacity to find beauty in the world needn’t diminish, but can evolve and even be enriched.
